To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cardiac-specific overexpression in mice of TNF-alpha, an inflammatory cytokine, causes atrial fibrosis, contractile dysfunction, and arrhythmia.

TNF-alpha overexpression leads to atrial arrhythmia and atrial contractile dysfunction due to atrial fibrosis, and that atrial fibrosis and contractile dysfunction lead to abnormal Ca(2+) cycling that contributes to the initiation of arrhythmia.
TNF-alpha transgenic mice develop atrial arrythmias that are due to abnormal Ca(2+) and action potential propagation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of atrial arrythmias in a mouse with heart failure.
the mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis in heart failure.
the study of the mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmias in patients with heart failure and in animal models of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TNF-alpha mice exhibit atrial contractile dysfunction, increased fibrosis, and atrial arrhythmogenesis, and that the arrhythmias are initiated by slow heterogeneous conduction and Ca(2+)-handling abnormalities in the atrium of TNF1.
TNF-alpha induced heart failure leads to atrial arrhythmogenic substrate that is more severe in males and that is associated with abnormal Ca(2+) homeostasis and atrial contractile dysfunction.
the atria of TNF1.16 mice have a decreased ability to contract, which leads to a decreased ability to propagate electrical signals and an increased propensity to develop atrial fibrillation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TNF1. 6 mouse model develops a heart failure syndrome with atrial arrhythmia as a prominent feature.
TNF-alpha overexpression in the heart induces a cardiomyopathy with atrial fibrosis and contractile dysfunction that predispose to atrial arrhythmia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TNF-alpha overexpression in the mouse heart leads to atrial contractile dysfunction, increased fibrosis, and atrial arrhythmogenicity.
TNF-alpha overexpression causes atrial arrhythmia in a mouse model.
atrial arrhythmia is a common feature of heart failure and that atrial fibrosis is associated with the arrhythmia.
